clue.text: Nick New and Old Testament given by church

explanation.surface: A church supplies a copy of both Testaments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given by' just joins the pieces; 'Nick' is a verb-looking noun meaning a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A nick is a small V-shaped cut, the same as a small indentation.

clue.text: Obtain dental treatment which the whole country must pay for

definitions.text: which the whole country must pay for

indicators.note: treatment suggests processing or handling, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Dental work on the state that the whole nation pays for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment' signals the anagram of OBTAIN DENTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Government borrowing is owed by the state, so citizens collectively owe the sum.

clue.text: Topic requiring space in an article

indicators.note: in means the space goes inside the article

parts.note: the is the definite article
an em is a printer's unit of space

explanation.surface: A subject that needs room in a magazine piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requiring' is a link; EM is a typesetting space, the width of the letter M.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject or topic of a talk or piece of writing.

clue.text: Getting tough on ship, one tries to minimise leeway

indicators.note: on means the first piece comes before the ship

parts.note: tough means hard
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: Getting tough on a ship, someone tries to stop it drifting off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leeway' looks nautical, drift downwind, but here means latitude or allowance; 'Getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncompromising person allows others very little latitude or flexibility.

clue.text: Stance about backing topless adult epilogue

indicators.note: about means the stance word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a stance or posture is a pose

indicators.note: backing means the trimmed word is read from right to left
topless means the word adult loses its top, its first letter

explanation.surface: A posture described in some racy epilogue to an adult show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adult' looks like part of the definition's racy picture; 'topless' leaves DULT and 'backing' gives the reversed run that sits inside the stance word.
explanation.definitionFit: A postlude is a closing piece of music, so a musical epilogue.

clue.text: Paper Russian apparatchiks very dutifully admired for the leaders

definitions.text: Paper Russian apparatchiks very dutifully admired for the leaders

indicators.note: leaders are front-runners, so each word gives its initial letter

parts.words: Paper Russian apparatchiks very dutifully admired

explanation.surface: A Soviet newspaper that party officials faithfully praised for its editorials.
explanation.walkthrough: The initial letters of the first six words spell the answer, and the whole clue describes the Soviet party newspaper; 'leaders' doubles as newspaper editorials.
explanation.definitionFit: The official newspaper of the Soviet Communist Party was revered by officials.

clue.text: One has a handle on what Scotsman wears under his kilt?

definitions.text: One has a handle on what Scotsman wears under his kilt?

parts.words: One has a handle on what Scotsman wears under his kilt?
parts.note: the thing with a handle is a small dagger, tucked into the stocking worn below the kilt

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about what a Scot has under his kilt.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface teases the old joke about Scots' underwear; the dagger is tucked into the top of the kilt hose.
explanation.definitionFit: This small Highland knife forms part of traditional Scottish dress, carried in the sock.

clue.text: So this would be to entreat, as permitted

indicators.note: with so added, this answer would become the word for entreat, so so is removed from it

parts.note: to solicit is to entreat or beg
the clue word so, taken as written

explanation.surface: Begging is lawful, so it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says SO plus the answer would make a word for 'to entreat', SOLICIT; take SO away to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Licit means lawful or allowed, the positive of illicit.

clue.text: Swim with hot, skimpy beachwear — just the thing in middle of cruise

definitions.text: just the thing in middle of cruise

parts.note: a dip is a short swim
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
a thong is a very skimpy bikini bottom

explanation.surface: Holiday swimming in scant beachwear, ideal mid-cruise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of cruise' is the vowel pair UI in the word cruise, a gliding vowel sound; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The two vowels in the middle of cruise form a gliding speech sound of two vowel qualities.

clue.text: Get chase broadcast with repeat for this action film

indicators.note: broadcast suggests scattering, so these letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A thriller whose car chase gets shown again on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' signals the anagram of GET CHASE plus REPEAT; 'with' and 'for this' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1963 war film about a prisoner breakout is a classic of the action genre.

clue.text: Having old piano, come to play such as bebop or even skiffle?

definitions.text: such as bebop or even skiffle?

indicators.note: play suggests letters at play, moving around into a new order

explanation.surface: With an old piano, come and join the jazz or skiffle session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having' is a link; 'play' signals the anagram of O, PIANO and COME TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Words like bebop and skiffle imitate the sounds they name, making them sound-imitative.

clue.text: Left between ports with prow dropping low in the water?

indicators.note: between means the left letter sits inside, splitting the two port names
the prow is the front, so the port's front letter is lost

parts.note: Dover is an English Channel port
Aden is a port in Yemen

explanation.surface: A ship lies between harbours sitting low in the sea after its bow dips.
explanation.walkthrough: One word, 'ports', yields two harbours here; 'with prow dropping' trims the first, leaving OVER, and 'between' sets the L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel overloaded with cargo sits dangerously low in the water.

clue.text: It's swallowed by brown dwarf? On the contrary

indicators.note: swallowed by means the first piece is taken inside the colour word

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: Astronomy: something gets engulfed by a brown dwarf star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' belongs to the definition: the opposite of a dwarf. It is tempting to read it as reversing the containment, but the plain reading already works.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposite of a dwarf is a giant, which is what a titan is.

clue.text: I.e. plant mostly seen in rocky state?

definitions.text: I.e. plant mostly seen in rocky state?

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady or shaken, so the letters are jumbled
mostly means the word plant loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A plant that thrives on rocky mountainsides.
explanation.walkthrough: IE plus PLAN, from 'plant mostly', is rearranged; the whole clue also describes the plant, which grows in rocky places.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine plants are those adapted to grow on high rocky mountain slopes.

clue.text: Flower of a type rarely identified in France

definitions.meaning: a small scarlet wildflower of fields

definitions.text: of a type rarely identified in France
definitions.meaning: the Scarlet hero of Baroness Orczy's novel, elusive and never caught by the French revolutionaries

explanation.surface: A rare type of flower seldom spotted in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense alludes to the line 'that demmed elusive' hero, whom the French could never identify.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarlet one is a red wildflower and also the disguised hero of a novel.

clue.text: Pest that might have drilled holes in bark of oak?

definitions.text: Pest that might have drilled holes in bark of oak?

parts.words: Pest that might have drilled holes in bark of oak?
parts.note: bark is a sailing vessel, not tree bark, so the pest bores holes in an oak-built boat

explanation.surface: A tree pest boring through the bark of an oak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bark' looks like tree bark but is a barque, a ship made of oak timber; the creature is a marine boring mollusc.
explanation.definitionFit: This mollusc bores into submerged timber, damaging wooden ships.

clue.text: French language tested with computer-aided learning

parts.note: something tested and confirmed is proven
CAL abbreviates computer-aided learning

explanation.surface: A French course checked by computer-based teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link between the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romance tongue of southern France is the Occitan dialect of Provence.

clue.text: Carriage taking poor nun to new church

parts.note: a Poor Clare is a nun of the Franciscan order
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A carriage takes an impoverished nun to a newly built church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' is part of the order's name, Poor Clares, not a comment on wealth; 'taking' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarence is a closed four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage.

clue.text: Drink chap returned, see, soberly

indicators.note: returned means both pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink
Ed is a man's name, a chap
Ely is a cathedral city, and a see is a bishop's seat

explanation.surface: A man goes back for a drink and is observed behaving soberly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns both drink and chap together, giving DEMUR. A see is a bishop's diocese, here the Cambridgeshire cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting demurely means behaving in a modest, sedate and serious way.

clue.text: Neglect fashion as time goes on

indicators.note: goes on means the time letter is added after the first piece

parts.note: to fashion something is to forge it

explanation.surface: People ignore fashion as the years pass.
explanation.definitionFit: To forget a duty is to neglect or overlook it.

clue.text: Silly to steer nearer the wind in empty ferry

indicators.note: in means the sailing word goes inside the trimmed ferry
empty means the inside is cleared out, leaving the outer letters

parts.note: luff is the sailing term for turning a vessel's head into the wind

explanation.surface: It is daft to sail closer to the wind in an unloaded ferry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' clears the middle of ferry; luff is a sailing term most solvers meet only in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluffy can mean lightweight or frivolous, so silly in a soft-headed way.

clue.text: 201 Bishop takes reduced fee to perform consecration

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a reduced fee is a charge of less money

explanation.surface: A bishop accepts a cut-price fee for consecrating a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' joins the pieces: B followed by LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To bless something is to consecrate it, making it holy.

clue.text: Rapid elimination of candidates without weight

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the sifting word surrounds the weight letter

parts.note: a sift weeds out unsuitable candidates

explanation.surface: Weeding out candidates fast without weighing them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside' here, so SIFT wraps W.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift means fast or quick, a plain synonym.

clue.text: What often shows up as brown, purple or white?

definitions.text: What often shows up as brown, purple or white?

parts.words: What often shows up as brown, purple or white?
parts.note: map colours shade terrain by height, with brown hills, purple mountains and white peaks

explanation.surface: A riddle about something that shows up in brown, purple or white.
explanation.walkthrough: The colours are the shading conventions for rising ground; 'shows up' hints at height.
explanation.definitionFit: A map coloured by altitude uses browns, purples and whites for higher ground.

clue.text: Small number entering do damage to house on estate

indicators.note: entering means the number goes inside the damage word

parts.note: to mar is to damage or spoil
NO is short for number

explanation.surface: A few people break in and vandalise a country house.
explanation.definitionFit: A manor house is the main residence on a landed estate.

clue.text: The quality of trifles and fancies in icing is quite varied

indicators.note: varied means changed in form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Puddings and cakes with very different icings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is quite varied' signals the anagram of FANCIES IN ICING; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Trifles are things of little importance, so their quality is unimportance.

clue.text: Excessive praise of cook introducing milky coffee

indicators.note: introducing means the coffee is brought inside the cooking word

parts.note: to fry is to cook
a latte is coffee with steamed milk

explanation.surface: A chef praised to excess serves up lattes.
explanation.definitionFit: Flattery is insincere or excessive compliment-paying.

clue.text: Largely get tongue around your poem

indicators.note: around means the trimmed word goes round the other piece
largely means most of the word, dropping its last letter

parts.note: to lick is to touch with the tongue

explanation.surface: Learn to get your mouth round a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get' is a link; 'Largely' leaves LIC, and YR is a texting-style short form.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyric is a short poem expressing feeling, often sung.
